name: Brindlebrook
hints: You cleared the first battle. The shore road by the south gate still leads out to Lighthouse rock.
Tap the open door to go down and fight.
Take the brass key to the door under the bluff: up the steps, then east.
Find the chest beyond the pond.
Talk to the elder by the well. The road out of the south gate goes to Lighthouse rock.
Tap the ground to walk. Tap people to talk. Swipe or use Turn to rotate the view.

case: Back at my gate, where nothing has teeth.
Welcome to Brindlebrook. Quiet place, mostly.
If you hear humming up by the bluff at night, that is the old door. Nobody has opened it in my lifetime.
It has gone quiet under the bluff. For now.
The door is open. When you are ready, we go down together.
You found the key? Then up the steps and east, under the bluff. Mind yourself.
A traveller! Good. The sealed door under the bluff has begun to hum, and I am too old to go poking at it.
The miller hid its brass key in a chest beyond the pond, years ago. If you find it, would you take a look?

choose: Bless you. Look beyond the pond, where the trees grow thick.
Of course. I will be by the well when you change your mind.

merchant: Apples, oranges, and a cabbage that has seen better days.
I am still setting up. Come back when the shop is open.

then: You found the shiny thing! I knew it was there.
else: There is something shiny in the trees past the pond. Turn the view around and you can see it!

case: The stair below is quiet. The rest of the dungeon comes in a later build.
The stair drops into the dark. Something is moving down there.
A heavy door, sealed tight. Something hums faintly behind it.
The brass key turns with a heavy clunk.
The door swings open. Cold air rolls up from the dark.
Not alone, you don’t. Bram, you are coming too.
Knew I should have stayed at my gate.

road: The shore road runs down to a rowboat pulled up on the shingle.
You push off toward the light on the rock.
